vis.current: Interactive launcher of the Zuehlke MCP actor tree (02 section 8). output_folder (Path) is where the JSONL files go; empty means the output folder of the project folder (the folder holding src, found from this VI's own path with Strip Path). ZM-ROOT-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS {outputFolder, usePlaceholderHardware = F} goes through ZM-ROOT-writePrelaunchSettings into the root, and Launch Root Actor starts it (Actor Core panel not opened). The VI then returns; the tree runs until Stop is pressed on the root's panel. error out is the error of the launch.

Headless test launcher of the Zuehlke MCP actor tree (02 section 8; 03 section 2, runs R-normal and R-error). It deletes TestPackage.jsonl in the output folder and ZM-error_log.txt in the output folder of the project folder (where ZM-CU-log writes it); a missing file is not an error. Then ZM-ROOT-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS {outputFolder = output_folder, or the output folder of the project folder when output_folder is empty; usePlaceholderHardware = use_placeholder_hardware} goes through ZM-ROOT-writePrelaunchSettings into the root, and Launch Root Actor starts it (Actor Core panel not opened). After Wait run_time_ms it reads the errors indicator of the running ZM-ROOT-root.lvlib:ZM-ROOT-root.lvclass:ZM-ROOT-helperPanel.vi (Open VI Reference by qualified name, Front Panel, Controls[] by Label.Text, Value) into ui_errors, sends Normal Stop to the root, waits 1000 ms and counts the lines of both files (a missing file counts 0). lines_written = lines of TestPackage.jsonl, last_line = its last line, error_lines = lines of ZM-error_log.txt. error out = the launch chain, the panel read and the stop, merged. The project folder is the folder holding src, found from this VI's own path with Strip Path.

Override of Actor:Handle Error (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the communication manager. Call Parent first (43 from a normal stop is cleared by the parent), then the hook ZM-CM-evaluateError on the class and the parent's error. By decision D40 (2026-10-11, errors are not handled yet) evaluateError is a pass-through: no log, no error package, no clearing; an error stops the CM, and its Last Ack carries the error to the root, which stops the root and the tree. stop actor? comes from Call Parent (af-shapes.handle-error-order).

Override of Actor:Pre Launch Init (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the communication manager. Call Parent, then the hook ZM-CM-createResources: it initialises the protocol from the pre-launch settings (ZM-CP-init) and writes it into the protocol field; if the init fails, it releases what was opened (ZM-CM-releaseProtocol) and returns the original error, so the launch fails with that error and Stop Core does not run (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup).

Override of Actor:Stop Core (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the communication manager. Call Parent first (the parent stops the auto-stop nested actors), then the hook ZM-CM-releaseProtocol closes the protocol (ZM-CP-close): code 1 from a never-opened resource is cleared without a log, any other release error is logged with ZM-CU-log and passed on by the hook (D44); the hook's error out ends here in Clear Errors, because AF's Stop Core has no error out (af-shapes.stop-core-order, errors.release-errors).

Hook of the communication manager (static, private), the one creating hook of Pre Launch Init (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.prelaunch-settings, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): Read prelaunchSettings -> Unbundle protocol -> ZM-CP-init (dynamic dispatch; the file logger creates its folder, the UDP sender opens its socket) -> Write protocol. Write protocol takes the read's error, not init's, so a partly initialised protocol is stored even when init failed; the two errors are merged (init's first). A case on that error: Error frame -> releaseProtocol on a fresh error chain (Stop Core does not run after a failed Pre Launch Init), then Merge Errors keeps the original error first; No Error frame -> pass through. Returns the error, so a failed create fails the launch.

Hook of the communication manager (static, private), called by the Handle Error override after Call Parent and by a helper loop after its loops. A PASS-THROUGH by decision D40 (2026-10-11: errors are not handled yet): the class, error in and stop actor? in go out unchanged; no log, no error package, no clearing. Shutdown and errors are controlled by the normal stops (an error stops the actor and, through its Last Ack, its caller).

Hook of the communication manager (static, private), called by Stop Core after Call Parent (af-shapes.stop-core-order) and by createResources after a failed init (af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): Read protocol -> ZM-CP-close (dynamic dispatch) -> Write protocol. Release errors (errors.release-errors): code 1 (UDP Close on a socket that was never opened, measured 2026-10-11 on a never-initialised MX [FL, UDP-sender]) is cleared without logging; any other close error is logged with ZM-CU-log as CM<tab>code<tab>source and then passed on (D44): error out = Merge Errors(the close error with code 1 removed by Clear Errors, then Write protocol's error out, which carries a failure of the log).
Public custom accessor: writes the pre-launch settings (af-shapes.prelaunch-settings); the caller fills ZM-CM-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS and launches the actor.

Override of Actor:Actor Core (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the hardware manager. ZM-HWM-init runs in series before Call Parent on the class and error wires (D41): it registers for the stop user event, so the registration exists before Call Parent can return, and its error goes into Call Parent. ZM-HWM-helperAcquisition runs beside Call Parent on the class input, a copy of the actor (af-shapes.helper-loop-vi), with the registration refnum from ZM-HWM-init. After Call Parent (the message loop has ended), ZM-HWM-stop fires the stop user event on a fresh error chain, with the class wire from before Call Parent (af-shapes.stop-site). Merge Errors (loop error out, stop error out) feeds ZM-HWM-close, which destroys the events after both (af-shapes.close-vi); Merge Errors (Call Parent error out, close error out) goes to error out, so a helper-loop error reaches the Last Ack (D40). No Stop Core override.

Override of Actor:Handle Error (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the hardware manager. Call Parent first (43 from a normal stop is cleared by the parent), then the hook ZM-HWM-evaluateError on the class and the parent's error. evaluateError is a pass-through for now (D40): the error is not logged, not sent and not cleared, so an error stops the actor and its Last Ack carries the error to the caller, whose default Handle Last Ack Core stops it too. stop actor? comes from Call Parent (af-shapes.handle-error-order).

Override of Actor:Pre Launch Init (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the hardware manager. Call Parent, then the hook ZM-HWM-createResources: it creates the stop user event (ZM-HWM-createEvents) and writes it into the events field; if the create fails, it destroys what was created (ZM-HWM-close) and returns the original error, so the launch fails with that error and Stop Core does not run (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup).

Override of the interface method ZM-CI-package_handler:ZM-CI-handlePackage (public, dynamic dispatch), called by the Do.vi of ZM-CI-handlePackage Msg: Read packageCount -> +1 -> Write packageCount; then Read Caller Enqueuer -> Send ZM-CI-handlePackage(package) forwards the package to the caller (the root). A failed send (the caller's queue gone during shutdown, 02 section 5) ends in Clear Errors; error out carries only the accessors' chain (Merge Errors with the cleared send chain).

Release member of the hardware manager (static, private), called in Actor Core after the helper loop and the stop (af-shapes.close-vi) and by ZM-HWM-createResources after a failed create (af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): Read events (fresh error chain) -> Unbundle By Name stop -> Destroy User Event -> Clear Errors. The release errors (an event never created, an invalid refnum) are ignored on purpose (errors.ignored-errors). error in passes through to error out (Merge Errors with the cleared chain).

Role member of the hardware manager (static, private), called by ZM-HWM-createResources in Pre Launch Init (af-shapes.events-typedef, af-shapes.resources): Read events -> Create User Event (Boolean, element stop) -> Bundle By Name into ZM-HWM-EVENTS -> Write events. One error chain; the error goes out so createResources can clean up and fail the launch.

Hook of the hardware manager (static, private), the one creating hook of Pre Launch Init (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): ZM-HWM-createEvents creates the stop user event. A case on its error: Error frame -> ZM-HWM-close on a fresh error chain (Stop Core does not run after a failed Pre Launch Init), then Merge Errors keeps the original error first; No Error frame -> pass through. Returns the error, so a failed create fails the launch.

Hook of the hardware manager (static, private), called by the Handle Error override after Call Parent and by a helper loop after its loops. A PASS-THROUGH by decision D40 (2026-10-11: errors are not handled yet): the class, error in and stop actor? in go out unchanged; no log, no error package, no clearing. Shutdown and errors are controlled by the normal stops (an error stops the actor and, through its Last Ack, its caller).

Helper loop of the hardware manager (private, static), started by Actor Core beside Call Parent with a copy of the actor; it talks to its actor only through Read Self Enqueuer and Send VIs. Its panel opens when called and closes afterwards. Two loops in this one VI: an EVENT LOOP on the stop user event, whose event registration refnum comes in on the pane from ZM-HWM-init (D41: registered in Actor Core before Call Parent, so no stop is lost) that exits on the event (writing the local stop = T) and a timed PRODUCER LOOP that calls ZM-HW-do every interval set (ms), sends the package to its own actor (ZM-CI-handlePackage), plots a test package on the live chart (temperature_c, duty_percent; any other package is skipped, its cast error cleared), shows the measured interval and exits when the local stop reads T after the Wait or on an error. Before the loops: stop = F and interval set (ms) = prelaunchSettings.intervalMs by local, ZM-HW-init on the settings' hardware. After the producer loop: ZM-HW-close (also on an error, safe state). Every loop stops the other when it ends for any reason (D40): after each loop the stop hook ZM-HWM-stop sends the stop event, its error ignored (Clear Errors); the event loop also writes the local stop = T. After both loops: Merge Errors -> ZM-HWM-evaluateError (a pass-through by D40) -> on an error Read Self Enqueuer -> Send Normal Stop to its own actor. error out is the raw merged error of both loops; the user event is unregistered here and destroyed by ZM-HWM-close in Actor Core. Error-handling plan: none yet (D40): an error stops this actor, and through its Last Ack its caller.

Init hook of the hardware manager (private, static), called in Actor Core in series BEFORE Call Parent on the class and error wires (D41). It does everything Actor Core sets up before the actor runs: Read events -> Unbundle By Name stop -> Register For Events on a fresh no error; the event registration refnum goes out on the pane to ZM-HWM-helperAcquisition, which wires it into its event structure's dynamic terminal and unregisters it after its event loop. So the registration exists before Call Parent can return, and the stop event that ZM-HWM-stop generates after Call Parent always reaches the loop (finding F14). The registration runs whatever error comes in; error out = Merge Errors(error in, Read events, Register For Events), so an incoming or a registration error goes on into Call Parent. Error-handling plan: none yet (D40).

Stop hook of the hardware manager (static, private), called in Actor Core right after Call Parent on a fresh error chain (af-shapes.stop-site): Read events -> Unbundle By Name stop -> Generate User Event (TRUE). The event loop of ZM-HWM-helperAcquisition then sets its local stop and exits. The error goes out to the Merge Errors before close.
Public custom accessor: writes the pre-launch settings (af-shapes.prelaunch-settings); the caller fills ZM-HWM-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS (hardware object, intervalMs) and launches the actor.

Override of Actor:Actor Core (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the root. Before Call Parent, ZM-ROOT-init runs in series on the class and error wires (D41): it launches the nested actors (ZM-ROOT-launchCm first, then ZM-ROOT-launchHwm, so the CM enqueuer is stored before the first package arrives; af-shapes.launch-owner, D6) and registers for the stop and error user events; a launch or registration error goes into Call Parent, so the root stops at once, and the registration exists before Call Parent can return, so the stop event always reaches the panel loop (F14). ZM-ROOT-helperPanel (the panel loop with the Stop button and the errors string) runs beside Call Parent on a copy of the actor with init's event registration refnum (af-shapes.helper-loop-vi). After Call Parent (the message loop has ended), ZM-ROOT-stop fires the stop user event on a fresh error chain (af-shapes.stop-site). Merge Errors (panel loop error out, stop error out) feeds ZM-ROOT-close, which destroys the user events after both (af-shapes.close-vi); Merge Errors (Call Parent error out, close error out) goes to error out. Errors are not handled yet (D40): an error stops the root, and AF's Stop Core stops the nested actors. No Stop Core override.

Override of Actor:Handle Error (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the root. Call Parent first (43 from a normal stop is cleared by the parent), then the hook ZM-ROOT-evaluateError on the class and the parent's error. By decision D40 (2026-10-11, errors are not handled yet) evaluateError is a pass-through: no log, no clearing, the error goes out unchanged, so an error stops the root and, through AF's Stop Core, the whole tree. stop actor? comes from Call Parent (af-shapes.handle-error-order).

Override of Actor:Pre Launch Init (protected, dynamic dispatch) of the root. Call Parent, then the hook ZM-ROOT-createResources: it creates the stop and error user events (ZM-ROOT-createEvents) and writes them into the events field; if the create fails, it destroys what was created (ZM-ROOT-close) and returns the original error, so the launch fails with that error and Stop Core does not run (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup). The children are launched from Actor Core, not here (af-shapes.launch-owner).

Override of the interface method ZM-CI-package_handler:ZM-CI-handlePackage (public, dynamic dispatch), called by the Do.vi of ZM-CI-handlePackage Msg. The root routes every package by its destination (01 R5): Communication -> ZM-ROOT-notePackageType, then, if Read cmRunning, Read cmEnqueuer -> Send ZM-CI-handlePackage forwards it to the CM. Root -> Read type: ErrorPackage -> ZM-ROOT-showError; any other type -> ZM-ROOT-notePackageType. Unknown, Hardware -> not forwarded, one line ROOT tab 0 tab dropped <getTypeName> for <getDestinationName> to ZM-CU-log; not an error. One error chain.

Release member of the root (static, private), called in Actor Core after the helper loop and the stop (af-shapes.close-vi) and by ZM-ROOT-createResources after a failed create (af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): Read events (fresh error chain) -> Unbundle By Name stop, error -> Destroy User Event x2 -> Clear Errors. The release errors (an event never created, an invalid refnum) are ignored on purpose (errors.ignored-errors). error in passes through to error out (Merge Errors with the cleared chain).

Role member of the root (static, private), called by ZM-ROOT-createResources in Pre Launch Init (af-shapes.events-typedef, af-shapes.resources): Read events -> Create User Event (Boolean, element stop) and Create User Event (String, element error) -> one Bundle By Name into ZM-ROOT-EVENTS -> one Write events. One error chain; the error goes out so createResources can clean up and fail the launch.

Hook of the root (static, private), the one creating hook of Pre Launch Init (af-shapes.resources, af-shapes.pli-failure-cleanup): ZM-ROOT-createEvents creates the stop and error user events. A case on its error: Error frame -> ZM-ROOT-close on a fresh error chain (Stop Core does not run after a failed Pre Launch Init), then Merge Errors keeps the original error first; No Error frame -> pass through. Returns the error, so a failed create fails the launch.

Hook of the root (static, private), called by the Handle Error override after Call Parent and by the helper loop after its loop. A PASS-THROUGH by decision D40 (2026-10-11: errors are not handled yet): the class, error in and stop actor? in go out unchanged; no log, no clearing. Shutdown and errors are controlled by the normal stops (an error stops the root, and through AF's Stop Core the whole tree).

Panel loop of the root (private, static), started by Actor Core beside Call Parent with a copy of the actor; it talks to its actor only through Read Self Enqueuer and Send VIs. Its panel opens when called and closes afterwards. One event loop (variant 1): the event registration refnum input (stop first, error second) comes from ZM-ROOT-init, which registers in Actor Core before Call Parent (D41, F14), and goes into the event structure's dynamic terminal; Read events gives only the error that seeds the loop's shift register; the loop carries its error in a shift register; Error frame: the loop stops; No Error frame: the event structure. Stop Value Change: Stop = F by local (Switch When Released), then Read Self Enqueuer -> Send Normal Stop to its own actor, and the loop goes on. error user event: the event's text is appended to the errors indicator, a newline between entries. stop user event: the loop exits (its only event exit). After the loop: Unregister For Events; the stop hook ZM-ROOT-stop sends the stop event, its error ignored (Clear Errors, D40); Merge Errors -> ZM-ROOT-evaluateError (a pass-through by D40) -> on an error Read Self Enqueuer -> Send Normal Stop to its own actor. error out is the raw merged error; the user events are destroyed by ZM-ROOT-close in Actor Core. Error-handling plan: none yet (D40): an error stops this actor, and through its Last Ack its caller.

Init hook of the root (private, static), called in Actor Core in series BEFORE Call Parent on the class and error wires (D41). It does everything Actor Core sets up before the actor runs: ZM-ROOT-launchCm -> ZM-ROOT-launchHwm (the class and error in series; each writes its enqueuer into the class) -> Read events on a fresh error chain -> Unbundle By Name stop, error -> Register For Events on a fresh no error (stop first, error second); the event registration refnum goes out on the pane to ZM-ROOT-helperPanel, which wires it into its event structure's dynamic terminal and unregisters it after its event loop. So the registration exists before Call Parent can return, also when a launch failed, and the stop event that ZM-ROOT-stop generates after Call Parent always reaches the panel loop (finding F14). The registration runs whatever error the launches give; error out = Merge Errors(launch chain, Read events, Register For Events), so a launch or a registration error goes on into Call Parent. Error-handling plan: none yet (D40).

Launch hook of the root (static, private), called from Actor Core before launchHwm (af-shapes.launch-owner, af-shapes.prelaunch-settings): Read prelaunchSettings -> outputFolder -> a ZM-CP-FL-file_logger constant -> Write outputFolder; a ZM-CP-UDP-sender constant with its defaults; both up-cast to ZM-CP-communication_protocol -> Build Array -> a ZM-CP-MX-multi_protocol constant -> Write protocols -> up-cast -> Bundle By Name protocol into ZM-CM-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS -> ZM-CM-writePrelaunchSettings -> Launch Nested Actor (auto-stop as AF's default) -> Write cmEnqueuer -> Write cmRunning = TRUE. One error chain; the error goes out to Actor Core.

Launch hook of the root (static, private), called from Actor Core after launchCm (af-shapes.launch-owner, af-shapes.prelaunch-settings): Read prelaunchSettings -> usePlaceholderHardware -> case: TRUE = a bare ZM-HW-hardware constant (the placeholder hardware, its methods return 5000), FALSE = a ZM-HW-SIM-simulated_hardware constant up-cast to ZM-HW-hardware -> Bundle By Name hardware and intervalMs = 500 into ZM-HWM-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS -> ZM-HWM-writePrelaunchSettings -> Launch Nested Actor (auto-stop as AF's default) -> Write hwmEnqueuer (kept for future commands to the HWM). One error chain; the error goes out to Actor Core.

Member of the root (static, private), called by ZM-CI-handlePackage for an ErrorPackage to Root: Read events -> Unbundle By Name error; ZM-PC-getDataAsJson -> Generate User Event (the panel loop ZM-ROOT-helperPanel appends the line to errors); To More Specific Class ZM-PC-EP-error_package -> Read data -> Unbundle sender; sender = CM -> Write cmRunning = FALSE (nothing more is forwarded to the CM). The only VI outside ZM-PC that knows the EP class. One error chain.

Stop hook of the root (static, private), called in Actor Core right after Call Parent on a fresh error chain (af-shapes.stop-site): Read events -> Unbundle By Name stop -> Generate User Event (TRUE). The event loop of ZM-ROOT-helperPanel then exits. The error goes out to the Merge Errors before close.

Public custom accessor: writes the pre-launch settings (af-shapes.prelaunch-settings); the launcher fills ZM-ROOT-PRELAUNCH_SETTINGS (outputFolder, usePlaceholderHardware) and launches the root actor.

The project's local error log (errors.log-local, D15): appends <ISO UTC timestamp><tab><message> to <project folder>/output/ZM-error_log.txt, creating the folder if missing; logs regardless of error in.

Creates an error package: a default ZM-PC-EP-error_package object, initialised by ZM-PC-init (dynamic), the data {sender, code, source} taken from the sender string and the code and source of error_to_report (an error cluster used as DATA, not the error chain), written through Write data, and the destination Root written through Write destination. The object is returned as ZM-PC-EP-error_package (To More Specific Class). Static, public.

Random test data for the simulated hardware (static, private). Five Random Number (0-1) draws: temperature_c = 20 + 10*r; sample_index = floor(1000*r) as I32; duty_percent = floor(101*r) as U8; sensor_ok = r > 0.1; status = {ok, warm, cold}[floor(3*r)] by Index Array on a string-array constant. The data output is shaped like ZM-PC-TP-DATA.ctl and bound to that typedef on the pane after generation. error in passes straight to error out (no node here raises an error).

Simulated-hardware override of ZM-HW-do (dynamic dispatch, own body, no Call Parent): ZM-HW-SIM-randomData makes a random ZM-PC-TP-DATA cluster, ZM-PC-TP-create wraps it in a test package, Write destination sets the destination to Communication, and the package leaves on the package terminal typed ZM-PC-package. The class wire passes straight from ZM-HW-hardware in to ZM-HW-hardware out; the error chain runs through every call. Stubs are swapped to the real members after generation.

Closes the hardware object (dynamic dispatch): writes initialized = FALSE through the private accessor Write initialized. This is where real hardware is put into a safe state (errors.default-policy); a child with real hardware overrides it and calls the parent.

Appends one line to a JSON Lines file (static, private): Open/Create/Replace File (open or create) -> Set File Position (end) -> Write to Text File (line + one LF, nothing else) -> Close File. Opened and closed per write, so every line is flushed (D3). The error chain runs through every file node into error out.

Builds the JSON Lines file path of one package type (static, private): file = Build Path(folder, type_name + .jsonl). One file per package type (D3); the name is the package's getTypeName. error in passes straight to error out (no node here raises an error).

Hook of the file logger (static, private), called by the ZM-CP-init override after Call Parent: reads outputFolder and creates that folder if it is missing (Create Folder; an already-existing folder, code 10, is cleared by Unbundle code -> Equal? 10 -> Select; every other error passes). Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent) so that the hook sits between Call Parent and the dynamic output of the override (trap T1 of 01b); inside, To More Specific Class casts the object to ZM-CP-FL-file_logger for the private accessor Read outputFolder. The class wire passes straight from in to out.

File-logger override of ZM-CP-publish (dynamic dispatch, own body, no Call Parent): Read outputFolder gives the folder, the package's getTypeName names the file (ZM-CP-FL-buildPath: <folder>/<type>.jsonl), the package's getDataAsJson gives the line, and ZM-CP-FL-appendLine appends it (open or create, end of file, line + LF, close) - one JSON Lines file per package type (D3), the protocol never looks inside the package (D10). The error chain runs through every call; the class wire leaves Read outputFolder unchanged. Stubs are swapped to the real members after generation.

Hook of the multi protocol (static, private, shared-clone reentrant), called by the ZM-CP-close override BEFORE Call Parent: Read protocols gives the array, a For loop runs ZM-CP-close (dynamic dispatch) on each element in order, with shift registers on the array and on the error, and puts each element back with Replace Array Subset at its index, so stopping never shortens the array; the loop stops at the first element error, which is returned. After the loop Write protocols stores the array from the shift register. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent, trap T1); inside, To More Specific Class casts to ZM-CP-MX-multi_protocol for the private accessor Read protocols, and Preserve Run-Time Class (target = the hook's input) returns the object that leaves Write protocols. Reentrant because an element may itself be a multi protocol (a static VI inside a dynamic-dispatch recursion).

Hook of the multi protocol (static, private, shared-clone reentrant), called by the ZM-CP-init override after Call Parent: Read protocols gives the array, a For loop runs ZM-CP-init (dynamic dispatch) on each element in order, with shift registers on the array and on the error, and puts each element back with Replace Array Subset at its index, so stopping never shortens the array; the loop stops at the first element error, which is returned. After the loop Write protocols stores the array from the shift register. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent, trap T1); inside, To More Specific Class casts to ZM-CP-MX-multi_protocol for the private accessor Read protocols, and Preserve Run-Time Class (target = the hook's input) returns the object that leaves Write protocols. Reentrant because an element may itself be a multi protocol (a static VI inside a dynamic-dispatch recursion).

Multi-protocol override of ZM-CP-publish (dynamic dispatch, own body, no Call Parent): Read protocols gives the array, a For loop runs ZM-CP-publish (dynamic dispatch) on each element in order with the same package fanned to every element, with shift registers on the array and on the error, and puts each element back with Replace Array Subset at its index, so stopping never shortens the array; the loop stops at the first element error, which is returned. After the loop Write protocols stores the array from the shift register. The protocol never looks inside the package (D10).

Hook of the UDP receiver (static, private), called by the ZM-CP-close override before Call Parent: Read connection -> UDP Close. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent), so the hook sits in series on the override's class wire (trap T1 of 01b); inside, To More Specific Class casts the object to ZM-CP-UDP-receiver for the private accessor Read connection. The class wire passes straight from in to out (nothing is written). The error chain runs Read connection -> UDP Close -> error out. Same name as the sender's hook, own class folder (02 section 7.8).

Hook of the UDP receiver (static, private), called by the ZM-CP-init override after Call Parent: Read localPort -> UDP Open on that port (default 61557, D25) -> Write connection stores the connection ID in the class. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent), so the hook sits between Call Parent and the dynamic output of the override (trap T1 of 01b); inside, To More Specific Class casts the object to ZM-CP-UDP-receiver for the private accessors, and Preserve Run-Time Class (target = the hook's input) returns the object that leaves Write connection (it now holds the connection) on the parent-typed output with the input's run-time class guaranteed, which the override's dynamic output needs. The error chain runs Read localPort -> UDP Open -> Write connection -> Preserve Run-Time Class -> error out.

Reads one datagram from the UDP receiver's connection (static, public): Read connection -> UDP Read with max size 65507 bytes and the given timeout_ms -> data out is returned as json (one JSON line per datagram, D24). A timeout (code 56) is cleared by Unbundle code -> Equal? 56 -> Select with a no-error constant and reported as timed_out = TRUE with json empty; every other error passes on and timed_out is FALSE. The class wire leaves Read connection unchanged.

Hook of the UDP sender (static, private), called by the ZM-CP-close override before Call Parent: Read connection -> UDP Close. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent), so the hook sits in series on the override's class wire (trap T1 of 01b); inside, To More Specific Class casts the object to ZM-CP-UDP-sender for the private accessor Read connection. The class wire passes straight from in to out (nothing is written). The error chain runs Read connection -> UDP Close -> error out.

Hook of the UDP sender (static, private), called by the ZM-CP-init override after Call Parent: UDP Open on local port 0 (any free port) and Write connection stores the connection ID in the class. Both class terminals are typed ZM-CP-communication_protocol (the parent), so the hook sits between Call Parent and the dynamic output of the override (trap T1 of 01b); inside, To More Specific Class casts the object to ZM-CP-UDP-sender for the private accessor Write connection, and Preserve Run-Time Class (target = the hook's input) returns the object that leaves Write connection (it now holds the connection) on the parent-typed output with the input's run-time class guaranteed, which the override's dynamic output needs. The error chain runs UDP Open -> Write connection -> Preserve Run-Time Class -> error out.

UDP-sender override of ZM-CP-publish (dynamic dispatch, own body, no Call Parent): the package's getDataAsJson gives one JSON line (D24: one datagram = one JSON line), Read remoteAddress -> String To IP and Read remotePort give the unicast target (defaults 127.0.0.1:61557, D34), Read connection gives the socket opened by ZM-CP-UDP-openSender, and UDP Write sends the line. Codes 66 (no listener, ICMP port unreachable) and 56 (timeout) are cleared by Unbundle code -> Equal? 66 / Equal? 56 -> Or -> Select with a no-error constant, so sending to nobody is silent (D25); every other error passes on. The protocol never looks inside the package (D10). The class wire leaves Read connection unchanged.

UDP receiver of the Zuehlke MCP data (02 section 8, 01 R9). A plain top-level VI, not an actor and in no library; it depends only on ZM-CP-UDP, ZM-CP and ZM-PC and can be started and stopped at any time while the actor tree runs (the tree does not notice). A ZM-CP-UDP-receiver constant gets port (default 61557) through Write localPort, then ZM-CP-init opens it. The loop calls ZM-CP-UDP-receive with a 1000 ms timeout: a timeout keeps waiting; a datagram is unflattened into ZM-PC-HEADER (not strict: the extra data key is ignored); for a TestPackage the data key is unflattened into ZM-PC-TP-DATA, temperature_c and duty_percent go to chart, interval measured (ms) is the Tick Count difference to the previous TestPackage (0 for the first), last line shows the received JSON and packets counts up. Any other package type is skipped. The loop ends when Stop (Switch When Released) is pressed or on an error; ZM-CP-close then releases the port. error out is the error of the loop and the close.

T3: test of the hardware hierarchy; Pass = AND of sim_ok, sim_destination_ok, ranges_ok, varies_ok and placeholder_ok. A ZM-HW-SIM-simulated_hardware constant on a ZM-HW-hardware wire runs init, do three times and close (sim_ok = no error at the end of that chain and every package's getTypeName = TestPackage); sim_destination_ok = every getDestinationName = Communication; ranges_ok = per package, getDataAsJson unflattened into a header+data cluster, temperature_c in [20, 30), sample_index in [0, 999], duty_percent in [0, 100], status in {ok, warm, cold} (Search 1D Array); varies_ok = the three sample_index values are not all equal; placeholder_ok = a bare ZM-HW-hardware constant's do returns code 5000 with source ZM-HW-do.vi: must be overridden by a child class (that error feeds the indicator logic only). error out carries the SIM chain's error. The two class seeds are path constants swapped to class constants after generation.

Calls ZM-CU-log twice with unique markers (T2-marker-A-<tick>, then T2-marker-B-<tick>), then opens <project folder>/output/ZM-error_log.txt (file_ok = the open succeeds), reads it whole, splits it into rows and tab columns, and checks that the last two rows carry the two markers in order (order_ok) and that both start with an ISO UTC timestamp matching the anchored Match Pattern (timestamp_ok). Reads <project folder>/output/ZM-error_log.txt before (a missing file counts as empty; that read error is cleared on purpose), then sends three test packages (ZM-PC-TP-create, Write destination) to handlePackage in series: Hardware, Unknown, Communication, then reads the log again. Each check counts a text in the log before and after (Search and Replace String, replace all): hardware_dropped_ok = more 'dropped TestPackage for Hardware' lines, unknown_dropped_ok = more 'dropped TestPackage for Unknown' lines, communication_not_dropped_ok = no new 'for Communication' text (a default ROOT has cmRunning F, so the Communication package is only noted, not forwarded), no_error_ok = error out is clean. T5: round-trip test of the UDP transport and the MX bundle; Pass = AND of rx_init_ok, roundtrip_ok, timeout_ok, no_listener_ok, mx_ok and rx_publish_5000_ok. Every protocol runs on a ZM-CP-communication_protocol wire (the parent's init, publish and close dispatch to the child). First output/test_mx_a/TestPackage.jsonl and output/test_mx_b/TestPackage.jsonl under the product folder (this VI's own path, tests and src stripped) are deleted (code 7, missing, is cleared). rx_init_ok = a ZM-CP-UDP-receiver constant with Write localPort 61557 runs init without error. roundtrip_ok = a ZM-CP-UDP-sender constant (defaults 127.0.0.1:61557) runs init; one test package (ZM-PC-TP-create with fixed data, Write destination = Communication) is published through it; the receiver's ZM-CP-UDP-receive(1000) gives json equal to the same package's getDataAsJson (string equality, the same object so the timestamps match), timed_out F and no error. timeout_ok = receive(200) again gives timed_out T and no error. no_listener_ok = after the receiver's close the sender publishes twice without error (codes 66/56 cleared in the sender). mx_ok = a ZM-CP-MX-multi_protocol constant with Write protocols = [FL(output/test_mx_a), FL(output/test_mx_b)] (each FL constant after Write outputFolder, up-cast with To More Generic Class) runs init, publish of the same package and close without error; both TestPackage.jsonl then hold exactly one LF and their line unflattens to the published package (timestamp, type, destination and the data cluster equal to the package's own JSON unflattened). rx_publish_5000_ok = publish on the closed receiver returns code 5000 (its own error chain, not wired into error out). Then the sender closes; error out is the main chain's end. The class seeds are path constants swapped to class constants after generation. Side effects: UDP on 127.0.0.1:61557; output/test_mx_a and output/test_mx_b with one TestPackage.jsonl each (git-ignored).

classes.current: Communication manager actor: owns a communication protocol object from its pre-launch settings, initialises it in Pre Launch Init (createResources), hands every package it receives to it (publish), and closes it in Stop Core. Error plan (D40, for now): evaluateError is a pass-through; an error stops the actor, and its Last Ack stops the root and through it the whole tree.

Hardware manager actor: owns a hardware object from its pre-launch settings; init registers for its stop event before Call Parent (D41); its helper loop ZM-HWM-helperAcquisition calls the hardware every intervalMs (init before, do in the loop, close after) and sends each package to this actor, which counts it and forwards it to its caller through ZM-CI-handlePackage. Error plan (D40, for now): evaluateError is a pass-through; the loops stop each other, a loop error ends the loop VI with the raw error and Normal Stop to this actor, and the error in its Last Ack stops the root and the tree.

Root actor: launches the communication manager (CM, first) and the hardware manager (HWM) from its Actor Core with their pre-launch settings, routes every package by destination (Communication -> forwarded to the CM while it runs; Root -> an error package is shown on the panel; Unknown and Hardware -> dropped with one log line), and shows its panel loop helperPanel with the Stop button and the errors list. Error plan (D40, for now): evaluateError is a pass-through; an error stops the root and, through AF's Stop Core, the whole tree; a child's error reaches the root through its Last Ack and stops it. init launches the CM and the HWM and registers for the panel loop's events before Call Parent (D41).
Message (made by Message Maker) that carries one package to an actor: Do casts the actor to ZM-CI-package_handler and calls ZM-CI-handlePackage. Send it with Send ZM-CI-handlePackage.
Interface: one method, ZM-CI-handlePackage; every actor that receives packages implements it.
An error travelling upward as a package: data = sender, code, source. Created by ZM-PC-EP-create with destination Root. init calls the parent, then sets type ErrorPackage.
A measurement package: the five-field data cluster ZM-PC-TP-DATA (temperature_c, sample_index, duty_percent, sensor_ok, status). init calls the parent, then sets type TestPackage.

Parent of every package. Carries a timestamp and a type (both written by init) and a destination (set by the creator). getDataAsJson produces the JSON; nothing outside the package looks inside its data.
Pluggable simulated hardware: do returns a random TestPackage addressed to Communication; init/close inherited.

Parent of every hardware object. init and close do real work on the initialized flag (close is where real hardware is put into a safe state); do is a placeholder that returns error 5000 and must be overridden by a child.
Pluggable file logger: one JSON Lines file per package type under outputFolder; init creates the folder after the parent; publish appends getDataAsJson to <getTypeName>.jsonl; close inherited.

Composite protocol: holds an array of ZM-CP-communication_protocol objects; init, publish and close go to every element in order, stopping at the first error, which is returned. The root gives the CM an MX holding [file logger, UDP sender] (D26).
UDP receiver: the reading side of the transport; receive returns one JSON line or timed_out. Does not override publish (5000 through the parent is correct, D25).
UDP sender: one JSON line per datagram, unicast to remoteAddress:remotePort (defaults 127.0.0.1:61557, D34). Sending to nobody is silent (codes 66 and 56 cleared, D25).

Parent of every communication protocol. init and close do real work on the opened flag; publish is a placeholder that returns error 5000 and must be overridden by a child. Never looks inside a package: it asks getDataAsJson and getTypeName.
